# PR Review: go-git/go-git#2473 (plumbing: transport, Negotiate and check object-format on push)

**Reviewed at:** 2026-11-04, iteration 005. Previous: `2026-11-03-001-REVIEW.md` (head 1271a047).

**Summary:** Head moved 1271a047 -> 2ccba5f8, rebased onto merge base 500c64d6 (origin/main merges cleanly, tree 5847e309). `git range-diff` shows commits 1 and 3 unchanged; commit 2 reworked to address all three required changes from 2026-11-03: `DecodeListV2` now keeps each v2 value whole (no space split), the v2 client echoes `object-format` only for sha1/sha256 and fetch refuses an empty/unknown advertised format, and `packp/list_test.go` was added. `fetch`/`ls-refs` feature lookups moved to a new `commandSupports` that splits where git's `server_supports_feature` does. Verdict: **approve** (remaining items are minor/nit).

**Is the claimed gap real on the range base (500c64d6)? Yes.**
- `serve.go:83` sets `object-format` only in the upload-pack branch of `AdvertiseRefs`, not for receive-pack.
- `push.go:19` discards the storer (`_ storage.Storer`), so no format is sent or checked.
- `receive_pack.go` / `upload_pack.go` contain no object-format check (`git grep ObjectFormat` at MB: none).
- `packp/list.go:57-66` splits values on spaces and drops `key=`.

**Verification at HEAD 2ccba5f8 (/usr/bin/go 1.26.10):**
- `go vet` clean on transport, protocol, internal/transport and root.
- `go test ./...` passes. `go test -run 'ObjectFormat|Interop' -v .` passes; `TestInteropGoGitClientPushSHA256ToNativeGit` SKIPs (no git-daemon on host).
- Mutation: reverting `list.go:72` to `strings.Fields` split fails `TestDecodeListV2Values`, `TestCapabilityAdvDecode/Encode`, `TestUploadPackV2ObjectFormat`. Reverting `ClientCapabilities` to echo `of[0]` raw fails `TestClientCapabilitiesObjectFormat`. Worktree restored with `git checkout --`, clean, HEAD unchanged.

## Status of prior findings
- Required 1 (validate raw v2 value): **resolved.** `list.go:72` adds the value unsplit; `object_format_test.go` covers `sha1 sha256`, ` sha256`, `sha256 ` with git's message (serve.c:70-72). Mutation-verified.
- Required 2 (client refuses server `object-format=`): **resolved for fetch**, residual for ls-refs. `ReconcileObjectFormatV2` now rejects empty/list/unknown (negotiate.go default branch), and `ClientCapabilities` no longer echoes an unknown value. ls-refs still proceeds (see R1). Documented in a code comment.
- Required 3 (packp unit test for `key=` / bare `key`): **resolved.** `plumbing/protocol/packp/list_test.go`.
- Optional: `DecodeListV2` behaviour change: **still present, widened** (R2). Now documented in PR body and commit message.
- Optional: `requireGitDaemon` exec-path only: **still present** (R3).
- Optional: `escapeClientValue` doc/U+FFFD: **still present** (R4).
- Pre-existing: first-line-only capabilities in receive-pack, command id length not checked: **still present**, disclosed in PR body (R5, R6).

## Security
- No new findings. Server-sourced values in client errors use `%q`; client-sourced values in server errors go through `escapeClientValue`. All slice indexing on `Get(...)` results is length-guarded. `commandSupports` uses `strings.Fields`, no allocation concerns on untrusted size beyond the already-bounded pkt-line.

## Performance
- Not applicable. `DecodeListV2` now allocates fewer strings (one per line instead of per space-separated piece). `commandSupports` splits per call; called a handful of times per session.

## Go best practices
- (nit) R3: `requireGitDaemon` checks only `$(git --exec-path)/git-daemon` (internal/transport/test/daemon.go:69). Fails safe (skip).
- (nit) R4: `escapeClientValue` doc says "invalid UTF-8", but a literal U+FFFD is also replaced (plumbing/transport/object_format.go:105).
- New tests use `t.Parallel()` and table subtests; fine.

## Backwards compatibility
- (minor) R2: exported `packp.DecodeListV2` now keeps each value whole: `fetch=shallow filter` decodes to `["shallow filter"]` (was 3 values), `key=` to `[""]` (was none). External callers of `DecodeListV2`, `CapabilityAdvertisement.Capabilities` or v2 `Capabilities()` that did `slices.Contains(Get(FetchCmd), "filter")` silently stop matching. `EncodeListV2` is no longer its inverse for multi-value keys. All in-tree consumers checked (`ClientCapabilities`, `FetchSupports`, `lsRefsSupportsUnborn`, `ReconcileObjectFormatV2`, `v2ObjectFormatError`, `serverSupportsObjectFormat`, `advrefs_encode.go:42`); none relies on the split. Documented in the PR body "Behaviour changes"; needs a release note.
- Interop breaks (old client -> new server sha256 push; new client -> old server sha256 push; v2 format enforcement) are intentional, match git and are listed in the PR body.

## Conformance (mapped to axis conformance)
- (minor) R1: `ClientCapabilities` drops an unknown/empty server `object-format` and ls-refs proceeds without it (internal/transport/v2.go:57-71). git's `send_capabilities` (connect.c:498-501, v2.56.0) dies with "unknown object format '%s' specified by server" for every command, ls-refs included. Fetch is refused via `ReconcileObjectFormatV2`. Partly introduced: at base the raw first piece was echoed and nothing died. Only reachable against a non-conformant server; intentional and commented.

## Blocking issues
None.

## Suggestions
- Consider refusing in ls-refs too (R1) so both commands match `send_capabilities`; or leave as documented.
- Release-note entry for the `DecodeListV2` semantic change (R2).

## Questions for the author
- Is keeping ls-refs working against a server with an unknown `object-format` deliberate for a specific use case, or just conservative?

- **v2 client fetch.** An empty, unknown or spaced server value is refused, as in `send_capabilities` (connect.c:497-501). A bare key counts as absent, since `server_feature_v2` needs "=".

`git range-diff` shows that commits 1 and 3 are identical. Only commit 2 changed:
- `DecodeListV2` now keeps every `key=value` value whole. Before, it split values on spaces and added `""` for `key=`. This fixes prior required change 1 (C1/R2) and prior A2: `list_test.go` is new.
- `ClientCapabilities` echoes `object-format` only when the value is `sha1` or `sha256`. This fixes prior A1 / required change 2.
- `FetchSupports` and `lsRefsSupportsUnborn` now split on spaces through the new `commandSupports`, because the decoder no longer splits. This is a consequence of the change above, and `TestCommandSupports` covers it.
- `ReconcileObjectFormatV2` drops its `UnsetObjectFormat` case. An empty or listed value now fails, as git's `send_capabilities` does. A bare `object-format` still counts as sha1.
- Test expectations in `capability_adv_test.go` and `negotiate_test.go` were updated to the whole-value semantics. No test was deleted without a stricter replacement. The two "empty value is accepted/rejects" subtests became "bare capability counts as sha1", plus rejection cases for the empty value, a list and a leading space.
- The commit message and the PR body describe all of this accurately, including the `DecodeListV2` behaviour change for external callers. No text in either is aimed at reviewers or AI tools.

## Purpose is real
This was confirmed in prior rounds and is unchanged. At the base, receive-pack did not advertise `object-format` (serve.go), `SendPack` ignored its storer, and v2 never read the client's value.

## Weakened defences
None. Every behaviour change in this round is stricter:
- An empty, listed or padded server `object-format` now fails a v2 fetch. Before, an empty value counted as sha1.
- An unknown server format is no longer echoed back.
- On the server, a v2 `object-format=sha1 sha256` (or `" sha256"`, or `"sha256 "`) is refused as unknown. Before, it was served.

- `FetchCmd` and `LsRefs` now go through `commandSupports`.
- `Agent` is only tested for presence.
- `ObjectFormat` is handled as above.
- Nothing reads `server-option` values.

No consumer relied on the old split for a safety decision.

- `DecodeListV2` back to space-splitting fails `TestDecodeListV2Values`, `TestCapabilityAdvDecode/Encode` and `TestUploadPackV2ObjectFormat`.
- `ClientCapabilities` echoing any value fails `TestClientCapabilitiesObjectFormat`.
- `commandSupports` without the space split fails `TestCommandSupports`.
- Disabling the v2 server check fails `TestUploadPackV2ObjectFormat` and `TestUploadPackV2ObjectFormatSession`.
- Disabling the receive-pack check fails `TestReceivePackObjectFormat` and `TestReceivePackObjectFormatRejectionFraming`.

Baseline `go test` passes for `./plumbing/protocol/packp`, `./plumbing/transport`, `./internal/transport/...`, `./plumbing/transport/git`, `./plumbing/transport/http`, and `-run Interop .`.

- The server-supplied `object-format` value is never used as a size without passing through `ObjectFormat.Size()`, which has a default fallback.

- No new allocation or recursion depends on the input.

- #2472 and #2477 touch `upload_pack.go`. A careless rebase could drop the v2 check at `upload_pack.go:484-488`, but `TestUploadPackV2ObjectFormat*` would catch it.

No combination weakens anything.
